🚨 *new alert — needs human*  (score: 6)
Channel: alert-system  •  bug-type guess: unknown  •  alerts in group: 1

Symptoms:
  - DD monitor 299251404 ("Service tables-fields has a high error rate on env:prod") fired 2026-07-03T03:32:24Z, self-recovered
  - 3 errors / 148 hits (2.03% vs 1% threshold) in the 5-min eval window ending ~03:31Z — diffuse across 4+ unrelated message types (SaveFieldLegacyExtended Failed, FillViewBasicInfo Failed, Failed to Delete Table/View, Message Deletion Failed)
  - Explicitly does NOT match ki-2026-07-02-tables-fields-fieldtablenameref-null-linked-fields — that KB's signature (FieldTableNameRef Is Null, concentrated) had only 2 hits in this window vs 18+ per prior confirmed occurrence; match_kb.py's broad "monitors/299251404" clause was a false-positive candidate, rejected after ES verification

Trace IDs: n/a — not pulled this cycle (message-level aggregation only)
Likely cause: Low-volume overnight error-rate blip on a critical-path service (ms-tables-fields-api); no single dominant root-cause signature identified; distinct defect from the known FieldTableNameRef issue
Suggested next action: monitor for recurrence; if it repeats, pull fields.dd_trace_id.keyword to identify affected account(s) and confirm whether it's a new defect or monitor-sensitivity noise from low overnight traffic

🚨 *new alert — needs human*  (score: 5)
Channel: alert-system (degraded cycle — DD monitor sourced, no Slack MCP)  •  bug-type guess: unknown  •  alerts in group: 1
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Transactions` (`@transactions` / `#team-transactions`)

Symptoms:
  - DD monitor 295882894 ("[Rainforest] Webhook Traffic Outage (Business Hours)") went No Data at 13:01:01Z — zero inbound hits to `runtime-core-api` `POST /api/v1/payments/rainforest/events` in the last 1h, first-ever fire of this monitor
  - 7-day baseline shows this endpoint's traffic is naturally bursty/batch-shaped (dense clusters ~04:00Z/08:00Z UTC, then quiet stretches); multi-hour business-hours gaps of 4-24h have occurred at least 3 times in the preceding week without a monitor watching for it
  - Today's gap is ~5h and counting as of scan time (13:09Z) — on the long end of the historical range but not unambiguously outside it
  - No 5xx/error signal anywhere — this is total silence, not a rejection pattern (rules out the existing `ki-2026-06-18-rainforest-webhook-inactive-account-500` KB, which is about inbound 500s for inactive accounts, a different symptom)

Trace IDs: n/a — no requests to trace (that's the alert)
Likely cause: Ambiguous — either (a) monitor threshold too tight for legitimately bursty/batch Rainforest webhook delivery, or (b) a genuine upstream delivery stoppage. Could not distinguish this cycle: deploy-correlation check on `runtime-core` blocked (repo fetch HTTP 403, `methodcrm`-org `GH_TOKEN` access gap).
Suggested next action: confirm with Rainforest (external vendor) whether webhook delivery actually stopped ~08:20Z today; if traffic is confirmed merely bursty, retune the monitor's evaluation window (e.g. 4-6h) to cut false positives

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-03-ms-scheduler-api-seriesid-negative-recordid`
This is occurrence #126 (chronic pattern, 7+ days running).
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `CRM Experience` (`@customer-management` / `#team-customer-management`)
Playbook: 1) Confirm shape: DD monitor 302054543 in 'Alert', or ES query fields.dd_service.keyword:"ms-scheduler-api" AND fields.Error.keyword:"Failed to Get Series Id for record -1 in table Activity". 2) Compute error-rate ratio (errors/hits, last_10m) — historically marginal (~2.5% vs 2% threshold), not a severe spike. 3) Root cause is a code-level missing-guard bug in SeriesDataProvider.GetSeriesIdAsync (not account-specific) — as of this cycle it has reproduced across 6 distinct accounts, not just lafittesseafood as previously documented. 4) File/bump a defect for CRM Experience rather than re-diagnosing from scratch.
